column4: Visit note | 2025-02-24 12:30 PM | Dr. Shamima Nasrin, Ophthalmology | Patient: Shamima Kabir, 76, female. Mrs. Kabir states that she suffers from long hours of screen time, gritty burning eyes, and symptoms worse in air conditioning. She mentions the discomfort began after long gaming sessions at home in Barishal. She works as a homemaker. She reports no other major systemic illnesses. Examination shows tear break-up time 7 seconds, BP 112/70 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, weight 46 kg. Corneas are clear and eyelids are unremarkable. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-02-25 02:30 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Rakib Sheikh, 39, male. Mr. Sheikh reports experiencing tense muscles and poor sleep. He explains this has been worse since job insecurity at a company in Rangpur. He works as a fisherman. He has no known comorbid conditions. Examination reveals GAD-7 score 10, BP 135/80 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 85 kg. Mental state examination shows anxious mood with coherent speech and intact cognition. Assessment: Generalized anxiety disorder. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to practise slow breathing daily, reduce tea and coffee, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-03-02 03:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Sharmin Kabir, 35, female. Mrs. Kabir describes cramping belly pain and stools that switch between loose and hard. She states this began after a bout of food poisoning in Uttara. She works as a tailor and has a history of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Examination reveals pain score 6/10, BP 124/70 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 52 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild tenderness in the lower quadrants. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-03-03 04:30 PM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Tamim Patwary, 56, male. Mr. Patwary presents after noting a high reading on a pharmacy machine and no other complaints. He mentions this was noticed after a stressful month of overtime in Rampura. He works as a garment factory worker and has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Examination reveals BP 155/107 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 73 kg. Heart sounds are dual with no added sounds, and chest is clear. Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to cut down on salt, pickles, and dried fish, walk 30 minutes daily, and check blood pressure at home twice a week. Follow-up in 1 month with home blood pressure readings.

Visit note | 2025-03-05 12:00 PM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Mahmuda Talukder, 61, female. Mrs. Talukder reports itchy eyes, a runny nose, and sneezing fits. She notes her symptoms are worse since keeping a cat at home in Shyamoli. She works as an accountant and has a history of Essential hypertension. Examination reveals about 11 sneezing fits a day, BP 141/87 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 57 kg. Nasal mucosa appears pale and boggy. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.
